record.paper_title: Grothendieck’s inequality and completely correlation preserving functions - a summary of recent results and an indication of related research problems
record.original_question: Find a closed-form formula, or prove appropriate structural results, for the Taylor coefficients of the inverse of the complex Haagerup function z ↦ (π/4) z · ₂F₁(1/2, 1/2, 2; |z|²), whose inverse coefficients are needed for the complex-field version of the completely correlation-preserving-function approach to Grothendieck’s inequality.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, a closed form representation of the coefficients of the inverse of a Taylor series runs against a well-known combinatorial complexity issue (due to the presence of ordinary partial Bell polynomials as building blocks of these coefficients - cf. research problem 7.1 below for details), which in general does not allow a closed form representation of these coefficients, such as is the case with the inverse of Haagerup’s function D ∋ z ↦→ π/4 z 2F1(1/2, 1/2, 2; |z|2) in the complex case.

An even stronger problem appears in the complex case, since already a closed-form formula for the coefficients of the Taylor series of the inverse of the Haagerup function is still unknown (cf. [ 17]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and define the complex Haagerup function $h:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ by
$$h(z)\;=\;\frac{\pi}{4}\,z\,\, {}_{2}F_{1}\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2};\,2;\,|z|^{2}\right),$$
where ${}_{2}F_{1}$ is the Gauss hypergeometric function. Since $h$ is a smooth bijection from $\mathbb{D}$ onto its image and $h'(0)=\pi/4\neq 0$, the (formal/local) inverse $h^{-1}$ admits a power-series expansion of the form
$$h^{-1}(w)\;=\;\sum_{n\ge 0}\sum_{k\ge 0} c_{n,k}\, w^{n}\,\overline{w}^{k}$$
on a neighbourhood of $0$ (the appearance of $|z|^{2}=z\bar z$ in $h$ forces a real-analytic, rather than holomorphic, expansion).

Problem. Determine an explicit closed-form formula for the coefficients $c_{n,k}$ of the inverse $h^{-1}$, or alternatively establish structural results (e.g. recursions, generating-function identities, asymptotics, or sign/positivity properties) that characterize them. In particular, express $c_{n,k}$ in a form that avoids the combinatorial complexity introduced by the ordinary partial Bell polynomials appearing in the generic Lagrange-type inversion of two-variable real-analytic series.
artifact.status_search_result: A closed-form formula for the Taylor coefficients of the inverse of the complex Haagerup function appears to remain unknown. Recent works on upper bounds for the complex Grothendieck constant via completely correlation-preserving functions (e.g. the 2023 preprint on upper bounds for Grothendieck constants and CCP functions) still treat these inverse coefficients via Bell-polynomial / Lagrange-inversion machinery without producing a closed form, and the related quaternionic Haagerup-bound work also does not resolve the complex case.

status_evidence.title: Upper bounds for Grothendieck constants, quantum correlation matrices and CCP functions
status_evidence.snippet: Framework using multivariate Gaussian analysis, higher transcendental functions and combinatorics of inversion of Maclaurin series to recover Haagerup's bound; closed form for inverse Haagerup coefficients not given.
status_evidence.claim: Recent CCP-function literature still does not provide a closed form for the inverse complex Haagerup coefficients.

status_evidence.title: Haagerup bound for quaternionic Grothendieck inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Treats Haagerup-type bounds in the quaternionic case while referencing the still-unresolved complex inversion problem.
status_evidence.claim: The complex inverse-Haagerup coefficient problem is referenced as an outstanding issue.
